item.title: ‘Be adults’: Joe Root gets rid of England Test team’s midnight curfew
item.description:
A Shift in Approach: England’s Test Team Embraces Responsibility

Joe Root has abolished the midnight curfew for England’s Test team, signaling a significant change in approach under his leadership. The move comes after a series of incidents involving players, including Harry Brook’s altercation with a nightclub bouncer and the suspensions of Ben Stokes and Gus Atkinson for breaking curfew. Root, who returns as Test captain after Stokes’ retirement, believes that curfews are ineffective in promoting responsible behavior from players.

item.title: Rangers striker Chermiti out for 'significant period of time' with ACL injury
item.description:
Rangers Striker Chermiti Sidelined by ACL Injury

Rangers striker Youssef Chermiti will be out of commission for a significant period of time after suffering an ACL injury during Sunday’s loss to Hibernian at Ibrox. The 22-year-old Chermiti, who joined the club from Everton last summer in a deal worth up to £10m, went down in the first half of the match after colliding with the pitchside boards. He was forced to leave the stadium in a boot and knee brace.

item.title: Premier League 2026-27 preview No 3: Bournemouth
item.description:
Under Pressure: Bournemouth Faces Uncharted Territory in the Europa League

Bournemouth’s secluded, swish training base stood empty, save for the lingering presence of departing head coach Andoni Iraola, as his successor Marco Rose prepared for the monumental task ahead. The new head coach has a lot to live up to after last season’s sixth-placed finish, a feat that saw the club qualify for Europe for the first time. And Iraola’s parting gift was a testament to the respect between the two coaches – a cordial farewell that belied the immense pressure now on Rose’s shoulders.

item.title: Will summit encourage Scottish clubs to give youth a chance?
item.description:
A Call to Arms for Scotland’s Senior Clubs

In a stark illustration of the dearth of opportunities for young Scottish players, Rangers’ Robbie Ure made his debut for the club at the age of 18, only to be limited to a total of three minutes of game time that season. This meager exposure ultimately led to Ure’s departure for Anderlecht in Belgium, where he has since flourished, scoring 15 goals in 15 games and attracting the attention of Sevilla.

item.title: Liverpool owners close to £1.35bn sale of 30% stake to consortium including Jeff Bezos
item.description:
Liverpool’s Turbulent Summer Takes a Dramatic Turn

Liverpool owners Fenway Sports Group (FSG) are on the cusp of a £1.35 billion deal that will see a 30% stake in the Premier League club sold to a consortium including Amazon founder Jeff Bezos. The proposed sale, which has been months in the making, would mark a significant shift in the ownership structure of the Merseyside club and inject a substantial influx of capital into the business.

item.title: Crystal Palace and Everton agree Brennan Johnson-Dwight McNeil swap deal
item.description:
Swap Deal Unfolds: Crystal Palace and Everton Reach Agreement

Crystal Palace and Everton have agreed a straight swap for Brennan Johnson and Dwight McNeil, marking a significant development in the transfer market. The deal comes six months after McNeil’s partner, Megan Sharpley, publicly criticized Palace for their handling of the winger’s potential transfer to the club.

The swap deal sees McNeil, who was set to join Palace in February but saw the deal collapse due to a change in circumstances, now heading to Selhurst Park in exchange for Johnson. Both players are expected to sign four-year contracts with the option of an additional 12 months. A medical for both players is scheduled for Monday.

item.title: Rangers chairman expects up to five more signings
item.description:
Rangers’ Transfer Window Ambitions

Rangers chairman Andrew Cavenagh has expressed his expectation of up to five additional signings before the transfer window closes, despite the club’s struggling start to the season. In a meeting with shareholders, Cavenagh acknowledged that results are not meeting his expectations, with the Ibrox club having secured only one point from their two Scottish Premiership games under new manager Derek McInnes.

The club has already bolstered their squad with nine new faces this summer, but Cavenagh remains optimistic about their prospects, stating that he hopes three to five more players will join the team. This sentiment was echoed by chief executive Jim Gillespie, who described the appointment of McInnes as a deliberate effort to bring in a “Klopp-style manager” who would adopt a proactive approach to the game. Gillespie noted that McInnes had been a top target for the club for an extended period and that his style and culture align with Rangers’ vision for the future.

item.title: Hogh hits hat-trick as Celtic ease past hapless Kilmarnock
item.description:
Historic Hat-Trick Secures Celtic’s Impressive Victory

Kasper Hogh’s exceptional performance on the new grass pitch at Rugby Park propelled Celtic to a resounding 5-1 win over Kilmarnock in their Scottish Premiership encounter. The Danish striker’s first-half hat-trick, scored in the 2nd, 33rd, and 35th minutes, proved to be the decisive factor in the Hoops’ triumph.

The attendance at Rugby Park was 8,353, a testament to the enthusiasm of the home fans, who had been eagerly anticipating their team’s first match on the new grass pitch. However, their hopes were short-lived, as Hogh’s early strike, which came just 64 seconds into the game, set the tone for the rest of the match. The £11m signing nodded into an empty net after Engels’ cross, silencing his early critics and silencing any doubts about his ability.

item.title: Five-time Super League winner Makinson to retire at end of 2026 campaign
item.description:
A Legacy of Excellence: Makinson to Hang Up His Boots

Tommy Makinson has announced that he will retire from professional rugby league at the end of the 2026 Super League campaign, ending a storied career that has spanned over a decade and a half. The 34-year-old Catalans Dragons wing, whose birthday falls in October, has made a lasting impact on the sport, with a tally of five Super League titles and over 300 appearances for his former club, St Helens.

item.title: True Love seeks Prix Maurice de Gheest crown at Deauville
item.description:
Racing towards Glory: True Love Seeks Prix Maurice de Gheest Crown

True Love, the Aidan O’Brien-trained champion, is poised to take on the best of the best in the Prix Maurice de Gheest at Deauville on Sunday, with the Group One crown within her sights. The 1000 Guineas winner, narrowly touched off by Thesecretadversary last month in the Prix Jean Prat, has been a dominant force in the sprinting ranks, and her versatility is expected to serve her well in this challenging test.

item.title: Wales must learn from Bosnia loss in Euros bid - Rush
item.description:
Disappointing Start to the Year: Wales’ Task Becomes Increasingly Challenging

Wales’ bid to qualify for the Euro 2028 tournament hit a roadblock, as they failed to win any of their four matches so far this year. The team’s struggle to secure a spot in the summer showpiece in the USA, Canada, and Mexico culminated in a painful penalty shootout loss to Bosnia and Herzegovina in March. This setback has left the Welsh national side facing a daunting task in the remaining months of 2026, as they prepare to take on Portugal, Norway, and Denmark in Nations League A.

item.title: Mbeumo scores in encouraging Man Utd draw with PSG but Mount injured
item.description:
Pre-Season Momentum Gains Traction as Man Utd Draw with PSG

Manchester United’s pre-season preparations continued on a positive trajectory, securing a 1-1 draw against European champions Paris Saint-Germain in Gothenburg, Sweden. The encouraging result, tempered only by the injury to Mason Mount, serves as a testament to the team’s growing cohesion and resilience under new management.

Bryan Mbeumo’s late equaliser, assisted by Amad Diallo, salvaged a draw that had initially seemed destined for the visitors. However, the momentum had shifted decisively in United’s favour following Diallo’s impressive display, which saw him win the ball back high up the pitch and tee up Mbeumo for a fine finish.

item.title: Huddersfield Giants to leave home for Dewsbury amid major investment
item.description:
A New Era for the Huddersfield Giants: Leaving Huddersfield Behind

The Huddersfield Giants, a Betfred Super League side, have announced their intention to relocate to Dewsbury’s Flair Stadium from the 2027 season onwards. This decision comes after a period of uncertainty, during which the club had been seeking a permanent location in the Huddersfield area.

The Giants’ move to Dewsbury is contingent upon RFL board approval, but the club has already begun investing a projected £10m-plus in developing the ground. The upgrade will transform the venue, increasing capacity from 5,000 to around 8,000 spectators and creating a viewing area on all four sides of the pitch. The redevelopment will also feature refurbishment of fan concourses, significant upgrades to hospitality suites, new bars and food areas, player dressing rooms, and press facilities, elevating the stadium to Super League standards.

item.title: Fifa president Gianni Infantino denies claims Uefa paid off alleged ‘lover’
item.description:
Fifa’s Leadership Under Scrutiny

Fifa president Gianni Infantino has vehemently denied allegations that Uefa paid off a female employee who is said to have been in a romantic relationship with him while he was the organisation’s general secretary. The explosive claims, which surfaced in reports by The Daily Telegraph, have sent shockwaves through the world of international football.

Infantino, who served as Uefa’s general secretary from 2009 to 2016, has been at the centre of a brewing storm for several weeks, with criticism mounting over his plan to seek private investment in a company that would manage Fifa’s major competitions, including the men’s and women’s World Cups. The Uefa president has confirmed that a “departure payment” was made to the alleged female partner, along with covering the fees for an MBA course, citing that the payment was in line with regulations in place at the time. However, Fifa has categorically dismissed the allegations as “categorically untrue,” with a spokesman for the organisation stating that any insinuation of inappropriate conduct or violation of statutes or regulations is defamatory.

item.title: AFL boss Craig Drummond apologises over Geelong concussion waiver: ‘The club went too far’
item.description:
AFL Confronts Concussion Conundrum

AFL Commission chair Craig Drummond has issued a rare apology for the Geelong Football Club’s secret concussion deal with player Jake Kolodjashnij, admitting that “the club went too far” in including a waiver in the informed consent document. This development comes after a week of intense scrutiny, with the club scraping the waiver on Thursday and the AFL releasing a statement distancing itself from the agreement.

The controversy centers on a 2024 agreement between Geelong and Kolodjashnij, in which the player took on legal responsibility for any potential future head trauma. Drummond, who was Geelong’s president and on the club board at the time, acknowledged that the club’s actions were “extremely complex and sensitive,” but ultimately acknowledged that the waiver was a misstep. “Regardless of the player’s agreement, the club went too far in adding a waiver into an informed consent document, and it will be removed,” he said.

item.title: Hull surges up leaderboard with course-record 62 at PIF London Championship
item.description:
Hull’s Record-Breaking Round Stuns at PIF London Championship

Charley Hull’s remarkable course record 62 has catapulted her into second place at the PIF London Championship, leaving a trail of stunned competitors in her wake. The English golfer’s blistering performance has sent shockwaves through the Ladies European Tour (LET), with many hailing her achievement as a testament to her unwavering dedication and unrelenting passion for the sport.

Hull’s second-day heroics saw her break the course record set by compatriot Georgia Hall in 2021, and her round of 11 under par has joined an elite group of LET records alongside the likes of Haeran Ryu, Jessica Korda, Alison Lee, and Karrie Webb. The five-time LET winner’s incredible display was marked by a bogey-free round, with the highlight of her day coming at the first hole, where she sunk an eagle to set the tone for an unforgettable round.

item.title: Must-win Hossler fires 61 to lead Wyndham after day one
item.description:
Unstoppable Momentum: Hossler’s 61 Puts Him at the Top

Tom Hossler’s remarkable first round at the Wyndham Championship catapulted him to the top of the leaderboard, with a sizzling 61 that left the competition scrambling to keep pace. The American golfer’s blistering performance on day one at Sedgefield Country Club in Greensboro, North Carolina, set the tone for what promises to be a thrilling conclusion to the tournament.

Hossler’s 10-under-par 61 was a masterclass in precision and power, as he navigated the course with a mix of precision drives and clutch putts. His exceptional play was a testament to his unwavering focus and dedication to his craft. The 28-year-old golfer has been in top form all season, and this latest display has further solidified his position as a top contender for the championship title.

item.title: Norway call on Infantino to resign but Mexico & Argentina back Fifa president
item.description:
Rift Within the World’s Governing Body: Norway Calls for Infantino’s Resignation

Norway’s football association has taken a bold step by calling for the resignation of Gianni Infantino, the 56-year-old president of the Fédération Internationale de Football Association (Fifa), amidst controversy surrounding his plan to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors. This move comes as a significant escalation of pressure on Infantino, following withdrawals of support from several football associations, including England, Wales, Croatia, and Albania.

item.title: Who will exit Chelsea? How Blues could cut 41-man squad
item.description:
Chelsea Confronts Crisis of Excess: The Battle to Trim a 41-Man Squad

Chelsea’s new manager, Xabi Alonso, is facing a daunting task: whittling down a bloated squad of 41 senior players to a more manageable 25. The consequences of inaction are stark, with the Premier League’s 25-man squad rule looming large. The club’s precarious financial situation, tied to a Uefa settlement agreement, demands drastic action.

Chelsea’s reliance on a large squad, a legacy of their past successes, has been compounded by their recent failure to qualify for European competition. The absence of continental football has left them with an unwieldy collection of players, some of whom are not involved in the first team. Alonso knows that the situation cannot persist, as it would only serve to undermine squad harmony and create tensions among the players.

item.title: Bethell to miss Pakistan Test series as Pope recalled
item.description:
England’s New Era

Joe Root’s second stint as England Test captain begins with a three-match series against Pakistan, starting in Leeds on August 19. The team, seeking to turn the page on a difficult spell on and off the field, has undergone significant changes. Notably, Ollie Pope and Brydon Carse have been recalled to the squad for the first time since the disastrous Ashes tour of Australia last winter.

However, another key player, Jacob Bethell, will miss the entirety of the series due to a knee injury sustained during England’s ODI series against India in July. This setback has led to the inclusion of Essex wicketkeeper Jordan Cox at No 3, who made his Test debut earlier this summer. Cox’s promotion highlights the need for fresh talent to bolster England’s batting lineup.

item.title: Players hit out at A-Leagues’ conduct over pay offer: ‘Continues to erode trust’
item.description:
A-League Negotiations Stall Amid Allegations of Bad Faith

Players in the Australian Professional Leagues (APL) have expressed disappointment and frustration with the A-League’s latest pay offer, which was hastily taken to the media just hours after it was sent to the Professional Footballers Australia (PFA). The move has been criticized for eroding trust between the players and the league, with PFA chief executive Beau Busch accusing the APL of negotiating in bad faith.

item.title: Scarlets chief Daniels dismisses Ospreys merger
item.description:
Uncertainty Looms Over Welsh Rugby’s Future

Scarlets managing director Jon Daniels has issued a stark warning to the Welsh Rugby Union (WRU) over its plans to cut the number of professional teams from four to three by 2028, stating that the governing body must provide greater transparency and justification for its decision. The announcement has left Scarlets and Ospreys in a state of uncertainty, with the west licence either being awarded to the Llanelli-based side or the Swansea-based rivals.

item.title: Why Arsenal are signing Newcastle captain Guimaraes
item.description:
Building a Winning Midfield: Arsenal’s Ambitious Move for Bruno Guimaraes

Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta has made clear that the club must be ambitious to build on their Premier League title win, and the signing of Newcastle captain Bruno Guimaraes is a significant step towards achieving that aim. The 28-year-old Brazilian midfielder will join a new-look Arsenal midfield, bringing with him a wealth of Premier League experience and a proven track record of success.

item.title: Tottenham Hotspur battled relegation last season, but a busy summer transfer window could see the London club back in competitive form under Roberto De Zerbi - Tottenham Hotspur 2026-27 season preview
item.description:
Rebuilding Momentum

Tottenham Hotspur’s rollercoaster ride last season ended on a note of relief, with a last-day victory securing their Premier League status. The harsh reality was that it took a dramatic finale to salvage their campaign, which had been marred by inconsistency and a series of disappointing results. However, with a new season on the horizon, the London club is poised to bounce back under the guidance of Roberto De Zerbi, the Italian manager who masterminded a remarkable turnaround.

item.title: Quiz! Can you name every team to have won one of English football's top four tiers?
item.description:
A Legacy of Excellence: Unpacking the Rich History of English Football’s Top Four Tiers

In a testament to the enduring appeal of the beautiful game, a staggering 95 teams have claimed victory in one of English football’s top four tiers over nearly 140 years of history. This milestone is a reflection of the country’s rich sporting heritage, one that has been shaped by generations of passionate players, dedicated coaches, and devoted fans. From the early days of professional football to the present era of the Premier League and EFL, the top four divisions have been the stage upon which some of the greatest teams and players in English football history have etched their names.

item.title: Several athletes 'unaccounted for' after Commonwealth Games in Glasgow
item.description:
Unsettling Silence Erupts in Glasgow

Several athletes have been reported missing after the conclusion of the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, sparking a search effort by Police Scotland. According to reports from Uganda, four members of the country’s boxing team failed to rejoin their delegation before the scheduled return to Uganda on Tuesday. The disappearance has cast a shadow over the successful hosting of the Games, which drew nearly 3,000 athletes from 74 nations.

item.title: Barcelona sign Brazil forward Kerolin from Manchester City for club-record £1.25m
item.description:
A Record-Breaking Transfer: Barcelona Sign Kerolin for £1.25m

Barcelona have made a major coup in the transfer market, securing the services of Brazil forward Kerolin from Manchester City for a club-record £1.25m. The signing is a significant statement of intent from the defending European champions, who are understood to believe Kerolin has the pace and trickery on the ball to become a regular goalscorer in the Champions League.

The transfer fee eclipses Olivia Smith’s £1m move to Arsenal in 2025 and Melvine Malard’s £850,000 switch from Manchester United to Chelsea, making it the largest sum received for a sale by a Women’s Super League side. Kerolin, 26, was part of the City side that won the WSL title and the Women’s FA Cup last season, and was with the club for 18 months after arriving from North Carolina Courage in January 2025.

item.title: Record number of new managers for season like no other
item.description:
A New Era for English Football

The 2026-27 Premier League season has kicked off with a record-breaking nine clubs beginning the campaign under new permanent management. This unprecedented level of change has dramatically reshaped the league’s managerial landscape, casting a spotlight on the ever-changing nature of football’s most demanding role.

From Liverpool to Manchester City, and from Newcastle United to Chelsea, the scale of turnover has been breathtaking. Liverpool appointed Andoni Iraola after Arne Slot’s departure, while Manchester City turned to Enzo Maresca following Pep Guardiola’s decision to step down. Chelsea, meanwhile, opted for Xabi Alonso after Liam Rosenior’s ill-fated tenure came to an end. Bournemouth appointed Marco Rose after Andoni Iraola’s contract expired, and Nottingham Forest hired Oliver Glasner following Vitor Pereira’s dismissal.

item.title: Australian swimmer Isaac Cooper leaves leadership role after drinking session
item.description:
Leadership Falters: Isaac Cooper Steps Down Amid Commonwealth Games Controversy

Australian swimmer Isaac Cooper has relinquished his position as a leader within the country’s swimming team after a decision to prioritize a drinking session over supporting his teammates at the Commonwealth Games. The 22-year-old’s absence from the final night of competition in Glasgow and the subsequent team wrap-up meeting has been deemed a breach of team expectations.

Cooper, a gold medal-winning swimmer, was last seen drinking in Glasgow while his teammates were competing. His actions, as reported by the Sydney Morning Herald, have led to a statement from Swimming Australia, confirming that Cooper has voluntarily stepped down from the team’s athlete leadership group. This development has marred the conclusion of what was otherwise a successful Commonwealth Games meet, with a record 37 gold medals secured by the Australian team.

item.title: MLS investigates reports of antisemitic chants toward New England’s Dor Turgeman in Montreal
item.description:
Abhorrent Abuse on the Pitch: MLS Investigates Antisemitic Chants in Montreal

On Saturday, during a highly anticipated matchup between CF Montréal and the New England Revolution in Quebec, a disturbing incident marred the game. Israeli striker Dor Turgeman, who scored a crucial goal for the Revolution in the 36th minute, was subjected to appalling antisemitic chants from the home supporters. The chants, which included the phrase “free Palestine,” were loud enough to be captured by broadcast microphones.

item.title: West Ham co-owner Sullivan advised to stay away from home matches
item.description:
Stadium Safety Concerns Fuel Calls for Sullivan’s Absence

West Ham co-owner David Sullivan has been advised to stay away from the club’s home matches at London Stadium, following a joint investigation by BBC Panorama and The Times into allegations of sexual misconduct. The recommendation from the stadium’s management comes in the wake of fan unrest concerns, and Sullivan is expected to defy the request despite the club’s intention to facilitate his attendance.

item.title: Tale of two halves leaves Iraola with plenty to ponder
item.description:
Turbulent Transatlantic Debut

Liverpool’s United States tour came to a close in dismal fashion, with a 4-2 defeat at the hands of Leeds. The outcome, though disappointing, will undoubtedly prove instructive for manager Andoni Iraola as he ponders the squad’s depth and physicality. The disparity between the first and second halves was stark, with Liverpool’s usually imposing backline crumbling beneath the weight of Leeds’ attacking pressure.

The first-half display, on the other hand, was a masterclass in cohesive football. Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz, both making their return to action, formed an electric partnership that suffocated Leeds with their relentless pressing and precision passing. Luke Chambers, who has been touted as a potential solution to Liverpool’s centre-half crisis, impressed in an unfamiliar role, hammering home a goal from inside the box after a clever corner from Dominik Szoboszlai. The 19-year-old Trey Nyoni continued his outstanding pre-season form, providing a solid showing down the left flank and contributing to Wirtz’s beautifully crafted goal in the 40th minute.

item.title: Scottish Premiership: Aberdeen’s late double stuns Hearts, St Johnstone edge thriller
item.description:
Aberdeen’s Late-Game Resurgence Puts Hearts on the Back Foot

In a stunning turn of events, Aberdeen’s stoppage-time double has left Hearts reeling after a 2-1 defeat at Pittodrie. The late drama secured a win for the hosts, who had seemed destined for a first Premiership victory at Pittodrie in over a decade.

Wouter Vrancken’s side had taken the lead through Oisin McEntee’s first-half goal, only to be pegged back in the 90th minute by Lewis Mayo’s equaliser. The match appeared to be heading for a Hearts win, but Kevin Nisbet’s stoppage-time penalty, awarded after Stuart Findlay was sent off for denying a goal-scoring opportunity, sealed the win for the hosts.

item.title: Commonwealth Games day 10: Finucane wins fourth gold; New Zealand claim netball glory – live
item.description:
History in the Making: Emma Finucane’s Unprecedented Clean Sweep at the Commonwealth Games

In a stunning display of athletic prowess, Welsh sprinter Emma Finucane has made history by becoming the first athlete to win four gold medals at a single Commonwealth Games. Finucane’s incredible achievement was sealed in the keirin final, where she made a move on the final lap to take the gold medal, capping off an unprecedented clean sweep in all the sprint events she entered.

item.title: England defeated by Australia in netball bronze-medal match
item.description:
Commonwealth Games Netball: Australia Secures Bronze, Denies England Medal Hopes

England’s netball team, the Vitality Roses, suffered a comprehensive 68-50 defeat to Australia’s Diamonds in the Commonwealth Games bronze-medal match, leaving them to depart the competition without a medal.

A 19-10 Diamonds lead after the first quarter proved unassailable for England, who failed to mount a substantial challenge despite a promising start. The Roses, who had exceeded expectations after a tumultuous build-up to the tournament, ultimately succumbed to a 35-24 half-time deficit and a 13-goal lead that proved too great to overcome.

item.title: Podium sweep and relay gold cap Australia’s record athletics haul at Commonwealth Games
item.description:
Record-Breaking Day for Australia in Athletics

In a spectacular display of endurance and skill, Australian athletes dominated the track and field events on the final day of competition at the Commonwealth Games, securing a record-breaking seven gold medals and cementing their position as a force to be reckoned with in the sport.

The day’s proceedings got off to a stunning start with a one-two-three finish in the women’s 10,000m walk, with Jemima Montag taking the top spot ahead of Elizabeth McMillen and Rebecca Henderson. The trio’s impressive performance set the tone for a day that would see Australian athletes claim medal after medal.

item.title: Commonwealth Games 2026: athletics, boxing, netball and cycling – live
item.description:
Glasgow Unfolds: Commonwealth Games Athletics, Boxing, Netball, and Cycling – Live

In a day of electrifying action, the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow have delivered a multitude of highlights across athletics, boxing, netball, and cycling. Among the standout performances, one particular breakout star has captured the imagination of fans worldwide: the “mop man”, an anonymous cleaner who turned heads with an impromptu dance routine during a netball match at the OVO Hydro.

item.title: Norrie beaten by Shapovalov in Los Cabos semi-final
item.description:
A Promising Run Ends in Defeat

Cameron Norrie’s resurgence at the Los Cabos Open in Mexico came to an abrupt close on Saturday, as he fell to a 6-3 5-7 6-4 semi-final defeat against defending champion Denis Shapovalov. The British number two had been on a remarkable upswing, having lost just one of his last seven matches after a six-match losing streak.

Norrie’s promising form was swiftly derailed in the first set, as he was broken in his opening service game and struggled to regain momentum. Despite several opportunities to break back, he ultimately conceded the set to Shapovalov. The Canadian’s dominance was underscored by a stunning forehand return that sealed the opening set.

item.title: England beaten by New Zealand in netball semi-final
item.description:
England’s Netball Dreams Shattered by Silver Ferns’ Dominance

A blistering performance by the New Zealand netball team, the Silver Ferns, left England’s hopes of Commonwealth Games gold in tatters as they triumphed 61-54 in the semi-final at the Hydro in Glasgow. The Roses, who had ambitions of emulating their 2018 gold, were ultimately unable to overcome the might of their opponents.

The Silver Ferns’ prowess became apparent early on, with their speed and accuracy in passing the ball allowing them to establish a commanding lead. By the end of the first quarter, England found themselves trailing 16-11, despite a valiant effort from goal shooter Liv Tchine. Tchine’s initial success in drawing the match level at 3-3 proved a fleeting moment, as the Silver Ferns’ height advantage through shooter Grace Nweke began to tell. Nweke’s impressive form, which saw her score 23 goals from 23 shots, proved a significant factor in New Zealand’s victory.

item.title: Fifa scraps controversial World Cup investment plan
item.description:
Fifa’s Reversal of Fortune

Fifa president Gianni Infantino’s decision to scrap the controversial private investment proposal for the governing body’s major competitions is a marked departure from the trajectory that had set him on a collision course with the world of international football.

The Swiss official’s announcement, made in the face of widespread opposition from member associations and governing bodies, brings an end to a tumultuous week that has left the future of global football hanging precariously in the balance. The move is a significant concession by Infantino, who had previously insisted on pressing ahead with the plans despite mounting opposition from Uefa, Concacaf, and the Asian Football Confederation (AFC).

item.title: Georgia Hunter Bell outruns Odira to win Commonwealth Games 800m gold
item.description:
Tactical Mastery: Georgia Hunter Bell Secures Commonwealth Games 800m Gold

Georgia Hunter Bell has once again defied expectations, outpacing world champion Lilian Odira to claim the 800m gold medal at the Commonwealth Games 2026 in Glasgow. The 32-year-old English runner, who has come a long way from her part-time tech job and her early days as a teenager competing at the top level, demonstrated unparalleled tactical acumen in a performance that left many observers stunned.

item.title: Commonwealth Games 2026: Hunter Bell wins 800m gold; athletics and boxing on day eight – live
item.description:
Commonwealth Games 2026: Athletics Reigns Supreme as Hunter Bell Wins 800m Gold

Georgia Hunter Bell’s dazzling victory in the women’s 800m final has electrified the Commonwealth Games 2026, cementing her status as one of the most promising middle-distance runners in the world. The 25-year-old English athlete stormed to the finish line with a commanding lead, crossing the line in 1:59.81 to claim the gold medal. Kenya’s Lilian Odira and Australia’s Sarah Billings trailed behind, securing silver and bronze, respectively.

item.title: Premier League agrees proposal to share an extra £1.5bn with EFL clubs
item.description:
A Reset for English Football: Premier League Agrees to Share £1.5bn with EFL Clubs

In a significant development for the future of English football, the Premier League has agreed to share an extra £1.5 billion with clubs in the English Football League (EFL) over the next decade. The unanimous vote by Premier League clubs to support the “new deal for football” paves the way for a comprehensive overhaul of the financial distribution within the top four divisions. The proposal, which will now be presented to the EFL’s board for consideration, marks a crucial step towards addressing the long-standing issue of financial inequality between the Premier League and the rest of the football pyramid.

item.title: Pressley signs new Dundee deal but warns of pain ahead
item.description:
A New Chapter for Dundee

Dundee’s manager Steven Pressley has signed a new contract with the Scottish Premiership club, but the 52-year-old warns that the road ahead will be fraught with challenges. The details of the deal, reportedly a one-year rolling contract, have not been disclosed by the club.

Pressley, who took over as head coach in June 2025, had been in discussions with the club about a new contract for some time. The agreement marks a personal milestone for the manager, who has been living in Scotland without his family for much of the past year. His wife is now set to join him in Scotland, a prospect he describes as a welcome respite from the isolation that often accompanies the role of a manager.

item.title: Howe going as spending rules bite - troubles for Newcastle's Saudi owners
item.description:
Trouble Signs Emerge at Newcastle as Howe’s Departure Highlights Frustrations

Newcastle United’s ambitious plans to become one of the world’s top clubs have suffered a significant setback with the departure of manager Eddie Howe, a consequence of the club’s struggles to comply with Financial Fair Play rules and generate sufficient revenue to fund their spending. The Magpies’ Saudi Arabia-backed takeover in 2021 was supposed to catapult them to the pinnacle of English football, but recent developments suggest that the club’s owners, the Public Investment Fund (PIF), may be running out of steam.

item.title: Merson: Vini Jr is playing Arsenal
item.description:
Experience Amidst Ambition: Chelsea’s Transfer Strategy Under the Spotlight

Vini Jr’s high-profile transfer to Arsenal has sent shockwaves through the Premier League, as clubs scramble to strengthen their squads for the upcoming season. Amidst the chaos, Chelsea’s potential double signing of Jordan Henderson and Danny Welbeck has garnered significant attention, with pundits and fans alike weighing in on the merits of the deals.

Paul Merson, a vocal advocate for experience in the Chelsea squad, believes that Welbeck and Henderson will provide the necessary stability to guide the young team through the ups and downs of the Premier League season. “It’s priceless, experience,” Merson emphasizes, highlighting the importance of seasoned professionals who can lead by example and provide a calming influence on the pitch.

item.title: Gianni Infantino’s big World Cup sale and Fifa’s race to the bottom line
item.description:
A Disgraced Organisation’s Descent

Gianni Infantino’s bold promise to restore Fifa’s image and address its financial black hole has given way to a more disturbing reality. The organisation is now seeking private investment in the World Cup and other competitions, a move that has sparked widespread criticism from top football authorities. The proposed £7.5 billion investment would be used to expand football development funding, but experts warn that this is merely a euphemism for lining the pockets of Fifa’s president and select executives.

item.title: Shankland named captain as Rangers near Makhanya signing
item.description:
A New Era of Leadership at Ibrox

Lawrence Shankland’s appointment as Rangers captain marks a significant turning point in the club’s history, as the 30-year-old Scotland forward takes the reins from the departed James Tavernier. Shankland, who joined Rangers just two months ago from Hearts, where he also wore the armband and scored 88 goals in 171 games, has spoken of his pride and honour at being chosen for the role.

item.description:

Scotland assistant Steven Naismith has downplayed speculation linking him with the national team’s top job, emphasizing that he is committed to remaining part of the set-up regardless of who succeeds Steve Clarke. item.title: Fifa offers $40m if nations back controversial plan
item.description:
Fifa Under Fire: A Power Struggle at the Top of World Football

Fifa president Gianni Infantino has ignited a firestorm with a proposal to create a commercial subsidiary to run its major competitions, including the World Cup, and sell off stakes to external investors. item.title: Commonwealth Games 2026: Dolci grabs fourth gold, Evans claims glory for Wales – live
item.description:
Commonwealth Games 2026: A Night of Unprecedented Triumph for Wales

item.title: Celtic complete club-record signing of striker Hogh
item.description:
Celtic’s Statement Signing: Hogh’s Arrival Sparks Hope and Questions

Celtic have made a club-record £11m transfer signing of striker Kasper Hogh from Bodo/Glimt, a move that has sent shockwaves through the football world. The 25-year-old Denmark international has signed a four-year deal with the Scottish Premiership club, with Celtic holding the option to extend the contract by a further year. Hogh’s arrival is a significant coup for the Hoops, and fans are eagerly anticipating what he can bring to the table.

item.title: AIG Women's Open: Full R1 groupings and Royal Lytham tee times
item.description:
Tee Times Set for AIG Women’s Open, Defending Champion Miyu Yamashita Aims for Second Consecutive Title

The 50th AIG Women’s Open tees off at Royal Lytham & St Annes Golf Club in Lancashire on Thursday, with 144 players competing in the final women’s major of the year. Yamashita will be out in the late-early wave alongside world No 2 Jeeno Thitikul and Lauren Coughlin.

item.title: Rose Davies storms home to win Australia’s first Commonwealth Games athletics gold
item.description:
Australia Seizes the Spotlight at Commonwealth Games with Historic Athletics Gold

Rose Davies stormed to victory in the women’s 10,000m event, securing Australia’s first athletics gold medal at the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow. The 26-year-old from New South Wales kicked away from Kenya’s Diana Wanza in the final kilometre, crossing the finish line 10 seconds ahead of her closest rival.

Davies’ triumph marked a significant milestone for Australian athletics, with the country’s first gold medal in the women’s 10,000m event. The Novocastrian, who holds national records in both the 5,000m and 10,000m distances, attributed her success to her consistent training and growth as a runner.

item.title: 'Medal dream didn't come true but my other dream is fighting brain cancer'
item.description:
A Triumph of the Human Spirit

Scotland’s Archie Goodburn walked out to a thunderous ovation at Tollcross International Swimming Centre on Monday, his heart racing with anticipation. The 25-year-old swimmer had qualified for the Commonwealth Games final just 24 hours prior, a feat that would have seemed impossible given his circumstances. Goodburn had been diagnosed with brain cancer two years ago, at the age of 22, and was told he might not see his 40s.

item.title: Sabalenka & Djokovic to team up in US Open mixed doubles
item.description:
Star Power Dominates US Open Mixed Doubles Lineup

Novak Djokovic and Aryna Sabalenka are set to team up in the US Open mixed doubles, a move that has drawn significant attention and interest in the revamped event. The high-profile pairing joins a list of notable names, including Jack Draper and Jessica Pegula, Iga Swiatek and Casper Ruud, and Naomi Osaka and Kei Nishikori, all of whom have indicated their participation in the two-day tournament.

item.title: Manchester City hope Rodri will sign new deal as Real Madrid weigh up offer
item.description:
Manchester City’s Rodri Saga Takes a New Turn

Manchester City’s hopes for Rodri to sign a new deal have been complicated by Real Madrid’s interest in the midfielder. The Spanish club has revised its stance on Rodri following his impressive displays as captain of Spain’s World Cup-winning team, where he won the Golden Ball as the tournament’s best player.

Rodri’s contract at Manchester City expires in June 2027, and despite the club’s optimism about negotiations, Real Madrid is now understood to be preparing a bid. This development may prompt interest from other elite clubs, including Barcelona, which could move for Rodri after Frenkie de Jong’s medial collateral ligament injury ruled him out for months. Paris Saint-Germain, too, is known to admire Rodri.

item.title: Identical Roper twins win gymnastics bronze medals
item.description:
Commonwealth Games 2026: Identical Twins Make History in Gymnastics

In a breathtaking display of skill and determination, the Roper twins, Abigail and Emily, have etched their names into Welsh team history, each claiming a bronze medal in the Commonwealth Games gymnastics events. The identical siblings achieved this remarkable feat within a span of just a few hours, leaving their fans and fellow competitors alike in awe.

The first Roper twin to claim a medal was Abigail, who secured third place in the women’s vault event. This achievement not only marked a personal milestone for Abigail but also set the tone for her sister’s subsequent success. Emily, who had initially finished fourth in the vault, demonstrated remarkable resilience in bouncing back to capture a bronze medal in the uneven bars event.

item.title: Chiesa happy but wants new chapter at Liverpool
item.description:
A Divided Mindset: Chiesa’s Liverpool Dilemma

Federico Chiesa’s latest remarks have reignited speculation about his future at Liverpool, despite the Italian forward’s insistence that he is solely focused on the Reds. In a candid interview with reporters following Saturday’s friendly against Sunderland, Chiesa stated that he is “happy” at Anfield, but his assertion is tempered by the reality of his limited playing time and scoring record under Arne Slot.

Over two seasons, Chiesa has started just one Premier League game and managed only five goals in 50 appearances across all competitions. The 28-year-old, who joined Liverpool from Juventus in a £12.5m deal in 2024, has been a subject of discussion regarding his consistency in the Premier League. In June, Chiesa told La Gazzetta dello Sport that if he fails to find his footing in the league, he would consider looking elsewhere. This admission has been viewed by some as a veiled threat to his current employers.

item.title: England 'far off their best' in netball defeat to Australia in Glasgow
item.description:
Disappointing Display

England’s Vitality Roses suffered their first defeat of the Commonwealth Games on Sunday, succumbing to a 66-47 loss against reigning champions Australia in Glasgow.

The Vitality Roses trailed 18-11 after the first quarter and 35-24 at half-time before a series of handling errors helped Australia stretch their lead to 56-35 with 15 minutes left. Despite managing to win the final quarter 12-10, England were unable to salvage the game, allowing Australia to claim a convincing victory. Olivia Tchine was England’s top scorer with 23 goals, but her efforts were not enough to prevent the defeat.

item.title: Commonwealth Games 2026: Ramsay-Peaty bounces back, Australia beat England in netball, and more on day three – live
item.description:
Commonwealth Comeback: Australia Dominates Netball, Gymnasts Shine on Day Three

Australia’s netball team has asserted its dominance over England, securing a resounding 66-48 victory in Pool A. The win marks a significant comeback for the Australian side, which had been pushed to its limits in earlier matches. Ramsay-Peaty’s impressive performance was instrumental in the team’s triumph, with her skill and strategy on court proving decisive.

Meanwhile, in the men’s 60kg weightlifting event, Bin Kasdan Mohamad Aniq of Malaysia has taken the gold, setting a new Commonwealth Games record with a lift of 152kg in the clean. Rishikanta Singh Chanambam of India secured silver with a new Games record of 121kg in the snatch, while Joshua Amunga Mboya of Kenya earned bronze.

item.title: Liverpool start Iraola era in style to beat Sunderland but Gomez injury deepens defensive worries
item.description:
A Promising Start, but Defensive Concerns Linger for Liverpool

A 4-2 victory over Sunderland in Nashville marked the beginning of the Andoni Iraola era at Liverpool, but the new head coach’s first game was marred by a worrying injury to Joe Gomez, which left the team’s central defensive options looking alarmingly thin.

The game itself was a comfortable win for Liverpool, with second-half finishes from Dominik Szoboszlai, Federico Chiesa, and Lewis Koumas delivering a decisive blow to Sunderland’s hopes. The Liverpool players who took to the field in Nashville showed promising signs, with lively displays from Calum Scanlon, Kieran Morrison, and Koumas catching Iraola’s eye.

item.title: Norris puts upgraded McLaren on top from Hamilton in final practice
item.description:
McLaren’s Resurgence: Norris Puts Upgraded Car on Top

The tenuous grip on pole position held by Ferrari and Mercedes appears to be slipping, as Lando Norris’s remarkable display in final practice for the Hungarian Grand Prix has catapulted McLaren into contention. The 22-year-old’s blistering 1:17.939 on soft tyres has left Lewis Hamilton and reigning world champion Kimi Antonelli trailing, casting a shadow over the expected dominance of the Italian and German teams.

item.title: Premier League: club-by-club guide to transfer business so far – and what they still need
item.description:
Transfer Tectonics: A Summer of Movement in the Premier League

As the English transfer record continues to be shattered, with Elliot Anderson and Morgan Rogers making their moves, the Premier League is witnessing a summer of unprecedented activity. Gone are the days of Mikel Arteta frantically scouring the market for a striker; instead, the champions are focusing on bolstering their wide options, with the highly touted Christos Tzolis arriving from Club Brugge’s left wing for a staggering £24 million.

item.title: Waratahs spoil Fijian Drua party to claim third straight Super Rugby Women’s title
item.description:
A Title to Remember

In the sweltering heat of Ba, Fiji, the NSW Waratahs etched their names in history books with a resounding 34-17 victory over Fijian Drua in the grand final of the Super Rugby Women’s tournament. This triumph marked the Waratahs’ third consecutive title, with their tighthead prop, Faliki Pohiva, being named the player of the match. As the team celebrated their record-extending seventh Super W title, the Waratahs’ captain, Emily Chancellor, reflected on the challenges they faced and the significance of this achievement.

item.title: Van Veen edges past Wade to book Price SF showdown in Blackpool
item.description:
A Thrilling Turn of Events in Blackpool

In a contest that ebbed and flowed like a tempestuous sea, Gian van Veen edged past James Wade to book a semi-final showdown with Gerwyn Price at the World Matchplay Darts, being held at the iconic Winter Gardens in Blackpool. The Dutchman’s 16-13 victory saw him reach the last four for the first time, setting up a tantalizing encounter with the world No 3, who recovered from a 12-8 lead to rattle off four consecutive legs and reach his first semi-final at the World Matchplay since 2022.

item.title: Hamilton fastest as Ferrari dominate Hungarian GP practice
item.description:
Ferrari’s Dominant Day at the Hungaroring

Lewis Hamilton’s impressive turnaround in the second practice session at the Hungarian Grand Prix has left Ferrari as the clear favourites for the weekend’s crucial qualifying session. The seven-time world champion edged his team-mate Charles Leclerc to the fastest time, reversing a half-second deficit from the opening session into a 0.158s advantage.

The Italian team’s impressive one-two finish in the more representative afternoon session was a testament to their car’s adaptability and pace. Ferrari’s dominance was not merely expected, given the circuit’s unique characteristics, but the extent of their superiority has sent a clear message to their rivals. The reigning world champion, Lando Norris, was the nearest challenger, but his McLaren was still a significant 0.488s behind Hamilton’s time.

item.title: ‘Football can change a country’: Klopp sets sights high after unveiling as Germany head coach
item.description:
A New Era for German Football

Jürgen Klopp’s appointment as Germany’s head coach marks a significant turning point for the national team, one that promises to shake up the country’s football landscape. Speaking at his unveiling press conference, Klopp laid out his ambitious vision: to transform a fractured relationship between the national team and Germany’s public, and to galvanize the wider community through the power of football.

For Klopp, the stakes are high. As he acknowledged, Germany’s performance in recent years has been underwhelming, with the team failing to make it past the last 16 since their 2014 World Cup victory. The 59-year-old coach, who has spent the past two years as head of global soccer for Red Bull, believes that football has the ability to unite a nation, and he is determined to prove it.

item.title: Argentina behaviour after World Cup final was ‘intolerable’, says De la Fuente
item.description:
A Foul Reaction

Sunday’s World Cup final at New York New Jersey Stadium will be remembered for many reasons, but the actions of Argentina players in the aftermath of Spain’s victory have left a sour taste. For Luis de la Fuente, the Spain head coach, the behaviour of his Argentine counterparts was nothing short of “intolerable and unacceptable”.

The incidents, which were captured on camera and widely shared on social media, saw Argentina’s Nahuel Molina and Leandro Paredes attack Rodri and Eric García, respectively. Moreover, Paredes confronted Spain’s Gavi, sparking concerns that the situation could have escalated into more serious incidents. De la Fuente praised the exemplary behaviour of his own players, who were faced with these “acts of aggression and provocations”, and expressed surprise that the Argentina players, whom he had previously praised, did not seem to be similarly affected by the confrontations.

item.title: Gina Rinehart offers bonuses for Australian swimming medals as funding gap exposed
item.description:
A Lifeline for Australian Swimmers: Gina Rinehart’s Bonus Scheme Offers a Glimmer of Hope

Amidst the backdrop of a Commonwealth Games beset by high-profile withdrawals, a glimmer of hope has emerged for Australian swimmers. Billionaire Gina Rinehart has announced a bonus scheme for the country’s swimmers, in a bid to bridge the funding gap that has left many athletes struggling to make ends meet. The move is a significant development, one that has been welcomed by Australian swimming’s star attraction, Kyle Chalmers.

item.title: Manchester City coach to be appointed in international role, with Jurgen Klopp reunion on the cards: report
item.description:
Reunited and Ready for the Challenge

Jurgen Klopp’s decision to leave his role at the Red Bull group and take on the challenge of managing Germany’s national team is set to bring a familiar face back into his coaching fold. Lijnders, a Dutch coach who spent several years working with Klopp at Liverpool, is expected to bring a wealth of experience and knowledge to the role. During his time at Anfield, Lijnders played a key part in helping the Reds win the Champions League and bring the Premier League title back to Merseyside for the first time in 30 years. His appointment is seen as a significant development, given his close relationship with Klopp and the fact that he will be joining his former manager at the international level for the first time.

item.title: St Helens boss Rowley leaves club day before derby
item.description:
The Fall of a Powerhouse

In a dramatic turn of events, St Helens head coach Paul Rowley has departed the Super League club with immediate effect, leaving a trail of questions in his wake. item.description:

item.title: ‘The utmost respect for him’: Alex Ferguson pays tribute to Kevin Keegan
item.description:
A Legacy of Passion and Footballing Greatness

The passing of Kevin Keegan on Monday at the age of 75 has sent shockwaves throughout the football community, with tributes pouring in for the former Newcastle United manager who built a team that would be remembered as the greatest in the club’s history.
